# Audit of the drafts

*Generated by `scripts/pages/hypodraft_audit.py`. Each marked statement links to what it rests on.*

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-SCOPE">This audit reads each draft in `hypodrafts/` and each open problem in `openproblems/` as committed at `7c4dd30`, and [Z8](../hypodrafts/Z8.md "The attenuation budget is never partitioned"), first committed later, at `0138743`, against the standards in [`../AGENT_BRIEF.md`](../AGENT_BRIEF.md): what kind of thing a quantity is, a null computed rather than quoted, and the steelman rule.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-SCOPE "What this claim rests on")</sup>

Verdicts are **sound** / **needs a stated fix** / **has an error**. Only defects are listed. Nothing here rewrites a draft.

---

## Per draft

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-A1">**[A1](../hypodrafts/A1.md "Danish land-based nitrogen load") — not settled here.** Its scoping is right: it says its finding *does not show the attribution is wrong*, only that one published figure cannot be what shows it is right — and the chain it examines is the one [what the sea actually receives](../NITROGEN.md) sets out, where DK-QNP takes the field surplus as a key input. Whether it misses independent support for the attribution cannot be judged here: that support would be Windolf and colleagues' paired catchment-and-estuary study, whose text could not be read.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-A1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-A1B">**A1b — sound.** It states what a result would and would not license, and it names the field surplus a norm product.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-A1B "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-B1">**[B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") — needs a stated fix.** The design is strong: exposure enters only as the combined-vs-separate class of the nearest outfall and as an *a-priori* critical rainfall depth, so rainfall cancels in the contrast.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-B1 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-B1-EEA">**But its central data claim is unverified here.** Its data row counts a table of EEA bathing-water samples that nothing in this repository holds or queries, so every figure in that row, and its `shortTermPollutionSample` count, stands unchecked. **Fix:** mark the EEA row unverified until the table is fetched and counted.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-B1-EEA "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-C1">**[C1](../hypodrafts/C1.md "Stratification strength") — needs a stated fix.** It refuses the published iltsvind extent as a response on the ground that DCE's criterion puts stratification inside the response's definition; DCE define iltsvind by oxygen concentration alone and name stratified water as where it develops, so the extent is not circular by construction. Its choice of raw per-measurement oxygen stands on the design's own unit, the cast. Its null work is sound: it names a non-zero floor, the fully ventilated saturation, rather than assuming zero.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-C1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-C4">**[C4](../hypodrafts/C4.md "Baltic inflow events") — sound.** It checks the Gotland file's units and provenance against the source netCDF, states its permutation floor, and gives its effective event count among what the design would not license.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-C4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-C6">**[C6](../hypodrafts/C6.md "Water temperature and solubility") — sound.** It never uses the archived `oxysat_bed` as its outcome, because it is computed from oxygen, temperature and salinity and so shares inputs with the statistic, and uses it once, as a consistency check.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-C6 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-D1">**[D1](../hypodrafts/D1.md "Bottom trawling") — sound.** It breaks the productivity confound with a within-station fixed effect, fluorescence for the confound's time-varying part, and a substrate × effort interaction that the confound does not predict.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-D1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-D7">**[D7](../hypodrafts/D7.md "Storm-driven resuspension") — sound.** It says the *monthly panel* carries no turbidity while identifying `Turbiditet` in the raw CTD — those are not in conflict — and it models the Secchi censoring that differs between its arms, which this project's light analysis counts.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-D7 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-F3">**[F3](../hypodrafts/F3.md "Loss of eelgrass and macroalgae") — needs a stated fix.** It avoids the clarity-indicator circularity by using cover rather than depth limit, and states the part it could not remove. That part, the eelgrass light requirement, has no source here, so its adequacy call is only as good as a requirement nobody has pinned.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-F3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-G1">**[G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming") — sound.** It re-derived the station split on a rule it states, set the result beside the split on file, and called the split threshold-dependent. That is the correct handling, and the other drafts that use the split should have done the same.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-G1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-I1">**[I1](../hypodrafts/I1.md "Changing station network") — needs a stated fix.** It opens on the summer-peaked / year-round split carried on file as prior work, without stating the rule behind it or noting that [G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming") and [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") derived other splits. **Fix:** state the rule inline and cite the brief's stated convention, as one convention among several. Its own methodological work is sound: it dissolves the classification circularity by defining the balanced panel on *presence*, which is observable per era.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-I1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-I3">**[I3](../hypodrafts/I3.md "Changing sampling frequency and season") — needs a stated fix.** It records that there is no time-of-day column anywhere in the archive. That is true of the **CTD extract** and not of ODA as a whole: the water-chemistry extract carries a clock value per sample. **Fix:** scope the claim to the CTD extract.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-I3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-K1">**[K1](../hypodrafts/K1.md "Silicon depletion and the diatom-to-flagellate shift") — sound.** Its point that the satellite functional types cannot carry the hypothesis stands on the files' own note that each is derived from chlorophyll. Its claim that OBIS returns cell counts through a measurement extension remains unchecked: no phytoplankton counts are held.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-K1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-L3">**[L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") — needs a stated fix.** It classifies stations as summer-peaked or year-round on thresholds of the raw Rayleigh resultant length R, and states no minimum number of observations. Under such a rule a station with a single observation has the largest R possible and counts as summer-peaked whenever that observation fell in summer, so the split can measure scarcity rather than season. **Fix:** redo the split under the brief's convention, which classifies on Z = N·R² and calls a station year-round only when it has enough observations, or drop the split arm and rely on the core panel.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-L3 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-L3-HEAD">**The draft's headline is not touched by this:** it reports its no-trend simulation null on a fixed core panel as well as on the split arms, and the core panel does not use the split.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-L3-HEAD "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-Z8">**[Z8](../hypodrafts/Z8.md "The attenuation budget is never partitioned") — sound.** It extracted `TA M06` as a primary document rather than summarising it, and names its residual honestly: *so this yields a variance apportionment, not a budget*.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-Z8 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-A7">**[A7](../openproblems/A7.md "Sediment nutrient regeneration") — sound.** It downloaded and parsed the flux dataset rather than citing it, and reports none of its stations in the Kattegat, the Belts, the Sound or any Danish fjord: a negative it counted rather than asserted.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-A7 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-E7">**[E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products") — sound.** It pre-commits to a reclassification test that would make the file wrong.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-E7 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-J1">**[J1](../openproblems/J1.md "Transparent exopolymer particles and marine gel") — sound.** It took the new-metric option seriously, wrote the metric down precisely enough to be rejected, then rejected it for reasons it computed rather than by asserting absence.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-J1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

<span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-R6">**[R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") — sound.** It reports that Denmark had a written national method for its own variables and stopped running it, and it states a reclassification test in advance.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-R6 "What this claim rests on")</sup>

## What the set gets systematically wrong

1. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-W1">**Inherited figures are not re-derived, and the one convention that matters was written down in none of them.** [G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming"), [I1](../hypodrafts/I1.md "Changing station network") and [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") each split the stations into summer-peaked and year-round: [G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming") on the share of a station's months falling in May–October, [L3](../hypodrafts/L3.md "The trend depends on the start year") on thresholds of the raw resultant length, [I1](../hypodrafts/I1.md "Changing station network") on the split carried on file. **This is the applefication failure in its purest form: a category everyone uses and nobody defines.** The brief's section on stated conventions fixes one: classify on Z = N·R², and call a station year-round only when it has enough observations for the test to reject.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-W1 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
2. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-W2">**Absence is scoped to the search, not the world — except where it isn't.** [D7](../hypodrafts/D7.md "Storm-driven resuspension") gets this right (*the monthly panel carries no turbidity*), [I3](../hypodrafts/I3.md "Changing sampling frequency and season") gets it wrong (*no time of day* anywhere in the archive). The difference is a clause.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-W2 "What this claim rests on")</sup> <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-W2-RULE">Every absence claim in these files should name the *file* it is absent from, never "the archive".</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-W2-RULE "What this claim rests on")</sup>
3. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-W3">**Quantity kinds are named case by case, not by rule.** [A1](../hypodrafts/A1.md "Danish land-based nitrogen load") calls its attribution a residual, A1b calls the field surplus a norm product, [B1](../hypodrafts/B1.md "Combined sewer overflow") calls per-outfall discharge volume a model output and [G1](../hypodrafts/G1.md "Warming") names its estimator; [C6](../hypodrafts/C6.md "Water temperature and solubility") keeps a derived channel out of its outcome and [Z8](../hypodrafts/Z8.md "The attenuation budget is never partitioned") calls its residual a variance apportionment. The brief asks for the kind beside every quantity.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-W3 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
4. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-W4">**The open problems pre-commit.** [E7](../openproblems/E7.md "Pesticides and degradation products") and [R6](../openproblems/R6.md "Sulphide locks the iron that would hold the phosphate") each state in advance the reclassification test that would move them.</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-W4 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
5. <span class="claim" data-claim="C-AF-AU-W5">**Nobody checked anyone else.** The station split is a defect no single draft could show: it appears only when the drafts are read side by side. **This audit is the missing step, and it should run after every batch rather than once.**</span><sup class="claim-mark">[†](../CLAIMS.md#C-AF-AU-W5 "What this claim rests on")</sup>
